newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Zhenhai sees good growth on stable oil.
newsitem.headline: Zhenhai sees good growth on stable oil.

text.p: Zhenhai Refining & Chemical Co Ltd sees good profit growth for 1997 after the completion of an expansion project and on expectation of stable oil prices for the year's first half, chairman Zhang Jiaren said on Monday.
The China oil refinery reported a 13.5 percent rise on its 1996 net profit against an increase of 26.3 percent in 1995.
"As a refinery company whose profit base has been growing continouly, it is not certain that the growth can be maintained above 20 percent every year," Zhang told a news conference.
But Zhang said earning prospects looked positive this year.
The price trend for crude oil looked good so far for the year after crude oil fell to about US$19.5 per barrel on average in March from US$22-23 at the beginning of the year, Zhang said.
"We estimate oil prices could stablise at the current level or even drop slightly in the first half of the year, although there may be short-term fluctuations in the second half," he said.
Zhenhai processed a total of 5.94 million tonnes of crude oil in 1996, of which 60 percent was imported and 20 percent was Chinese offshore oil bought at market prices.

The company adopted various strategies to absorb the impact of an oil price increase late last year, including hedging, 24-hour monitoring of the market trend and increasing purchases of cheap heavy and Middle Eastern sour crdue oil.
The heavy oil plus sour oil accounted for about 37.8 percent of the total oil the company processed last year.
"They are relatively cheap and helped us to keep our crude oil cost in the fourth quarter (1996) in relatively good shape," the chairman said.
Prices for heavy oil and sour oil was about US$1-1.5 lower than light crude oil, he noted.
"This effectively minimised the pressure from price fluctuations to our company," Zhang said.
The overall oil cost last year for the company averaged 1,105 yuan per tonne, or nine percent higher than the average cost the previous year.

The company planned to process at least 6.7 million tonne of oil this year, up 10 percent from the previous year, following the completion of a capacity upgrading program, which lifted production to a maximum of seven million tonnes per year.
It also planned to produce more value-added products such as urea and use more Middle East oil to cut cost, Zhang said.
